content.title: About
content.content: Green snap beans are the young pods of the common pea (Pisum sativum) harvested before the seeds fully develop. They have a crisp texture, a mildly sweet flavor, and are rich in vitamins, minerals, and fiber. Beans are typically eaten raw in salads, as a snack, or added to dishes for crunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Snap beans belong to the legume family and are the precursor to larger pea varieties.
Edible pods are picked when they are still tender, usually 60–70 days after planting.
In Japan, snap beans are often served boiled as “edamame,” though the traditional preparation uses larger pods.
Vitamin K content in snap beans is higher than in most leafy vegetables.
Heirloom varieties may display a brighter green color and a sweeter taste.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, satiety, and helps maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Snap beans are low in calories, making them a good choice for weight management.

items.title: High in antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids in beans help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to legumes, including snap beans.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals; soaking lowers its level.

items.title: Possible contamination
items.content: Raw beans can be contaminated with bacteria or pesticide residues; thorough washing is recommended before consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Snap beans can be eaten raw in salads, added to smoothies, used as a crunchy snack, or rolled in sushi. If a softer texture is desired, briefly blanch them in boiling water, but raw consumption preserves the highest vitamin content.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store snap beans in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. They stay fresh for 5–7 days. For longer storage, freeze them in sealed bags where they keep for up to 8 months.
